purpose: systems feasibility, not benchmark -- no model-quality claim should be read from this file

preprocessing.adjacency_cpu_rss_mb_proxy_note: No dedicated pre/post-adjacency memory snapshot was instrumented. The closest available number is total process RSS at batch 0 (2460.79 MB), which already includes the Python interpreter, torch, the full 8,097,798-row triples array, the positive-triple store, type pools, the model, optimizer, and the first sampled subgraph -- not an isolated measurement of the adjacency structure alone. Treat this as an upper bound on everything loaded by that point, not as the adjacency's own footprint.
preprocessing.adjacency_caching_safety_reasoning: build_relation_adjacency() is a pure deterministic function of its input triples array (plain dict aggregation, no RNG draws), and in this pipeline it is only ever built from the already leakage-safe tuning_triples/final_triples. Caching its output (e.g. keyed by a hash of the input triples array) would not alter determinism or reintroduce any leakage risk -- it would only skip recomputing an already-deterministic, already-leakage-safe structure. No caching was implemented in this task; this is a reasoning-based conclusion from the existing code, not a measurement of an implemented cache.
preprocessing.adjacency_build_classification_reason: 12.97s to build the full-scale relation adjacency from all 8,097,798 real tuning triples is negligible next to both the measured steady-state per-batch cost (~5.2s/batch) and the resulting projected full-epoch runtime (~11.4 hours) -- adjacency construction is not the bottleneck.

steady_state_batch_timing_s.note: Computed over batches 1..499 (excludes batch 0, which includes one-time CUDA/model warmup). Units: seconds.
steady_state_batch_timing_s.bottleneck_finding: Neighbor sampling (CPU-bound, single-threaded Python/NumPy traversal of RelationAwareNeighborSampler.sample(), itself built on the plain-dict RelationAdjacency flagged as not-yet-scale-optimized in its own module docstring) accounts for ~96.4% of total batch wall time. GPU-side encoder forward, decoder/loss, and backward together account for under 3% of batch time. This is a severe CPU bottleneck, not a GPU compute or GPU memory bottleneck.

cuda_memory_mb.note: Computed over batches 1..499; peak_* are torch's running max since the last reset_peak_memory_stats() call (made once, immediately before this profile), not per-batch peaks.
cuda_memory_mb.progressive_memory_growth_over_batch_ind: none observed -- peak_allocated/peak_reserved plateau after the first ~100 batches and stay flat (max 656.66 MB allocated / 738 MB reserved across all 500 batches); no leak signature

cpu_memory_mb.progressive_memory_growth_over_batch_ind: none observed -- ru_maxrss is a monotonic high-water mark and it stabilizes almost immediately; no CPU-side leak signature over 500 batches

sampler_stats.note: Zero unresolved negatives across all 500 batches (2,048,000 negative draws) -- the vectorized-retry/scalar-fallback negative sampler never failed to find a valid negative within budget.

runtime_projection.note: Pure arithmetic projection from the measured steady-state mean batch time. Not a recommendation; the 3-config search is explicitly NOT launched in this task regardless of this projection.

feasibility_decision.classification_axis: runtime (CPU-bound sampler), not GPU memory -- GPU memory headroom is excellent (peak reserved 738 MB of 14,941 MB, 4.9% utilization)
feasibility_decision.reason: All 500 batches ran cleanly with no OOM, no NaN/Inf, and no progressive memory growth on either GPU or CPU -- the sampled-subgraph training architecture itself is memory-safe at real PrimeKG scale. However, neighbor sampling consumes ~96.4% of every batch's wall time, driving a projected full-epoch runtime of ~11.4 hours and a projected 3-config x 3-epoch search of ~103 hours. This is a severe CPU bottleneck producing an operationally impractical runtime for the planned validation search, which is explicitly one of this task's own C-classification triggers.
feasibility_decision.root_cause: RelationAwareNeighborSampler.sample() (rgcn_sampling.py), specifically the per-seed-entity, per-hop Python loop in _sample_subgraph_impl() and _sample_neighbors_relation_balanced() -- a correct but unoptimized plain-Python/dict implementation, exactly as flagged as a known risk in that module's own docstring before this profiling task began.
feasibility_decision.not_the_cause: GPU memory, GPU compute (encoder/decoder/backward/optimizer together are under 3% of batch time), adjacency construction (one-time 12.97s), negative sampling (0.5% of batch time), host-device transfer (0.1% of batch time).

next_step_note: Do not tune fanout, batch size, or sampling methodology in response to this profile, and do not start the 3-config search. The architecture is memory-safe but the current neighbor-sampling implementation is the practical blocker. A separately justified methodological decision is needed (e.g. vectorizing/batching the neighbor sampler, caching the deterministic adjacency across runs, precomputing neighbor lists, or a different sampling strategy) before any real validation search is attempted -- that decision is the user's, not an autonomous continuation of this profiling task.
